title: Corpus: add reordered-keys + trailing-bytes reject cases to gcp_slot_claim_cose_sign1 vectors
description: Found during l2uk review (security pass, kimi-k3). test/vectors/gcp_slot_claim_cose_sign1.json has 13 cases (happy_path, mutations, replay, expiry, decoy, kid-mismatch, ordinal_absent) but no non-ascending-payload-keys or trailing-payload-bytes rejection case. Rust now rejects both (l2uk); C rejects both implicitly (digests received bytes); Python accepts both (parity gap, filed separately). The project rule is identical verdicts on test/vectors/ across implementations — add both cases (plus generator support) so C and Python are mechanically cross-checked against the deterministic-CBOR rejection class; a Python corpus harness for these cases will go red until the Python decoder parity fix lands.
